summary: "ADVANCED 2026-07-30 by ajc-p3 (run 0085 r5): layer 2's ALGEBRA half is closed,\
  \ and the localized chart now HAS a quotient rather than needing one built. The\
  \ non-affine gate is NOT discharged. Owner still ajc-p3 while the round runs.\n\n\
  LANDED, DO NOT REDO. Picard/GaloisDescent/InvariantsLocalization.lean, rooted at\
  \ AlgebraicJacobian.lean, 10 declarations, ZERO code sorries, ALL TEN axiom-clean\
  \ [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] against fgaPicardRepresentability as a\
  \ control that fires sorryAx in the same run, with oleans rebuilt BEFORE the probe\
  \ (I-1057). lake env lean EXIT=0; lake build of the module EXIT=0.\n * powers_map_eq\
  \ -- gamma carries Submonoid.powers N onto itself. The ONE place invariance of N\
  \ is spent, and the reason the whole construction is about invariant elements.\n\
  \ * awayAut / awayAut_algebraMap / awayAutHom / awayAction -- the transported automorphism,\
  \ its value on the image of A, multiplicativity, and the action. Both action laws\
  \ are IsLocalization.ringHom_ext against awayAut_algebraMap.\n * isSemilinear_away\
  \ -- THE PAYLOAD: the transported action is semilinear, which is the hypothesis\
  \ of invariantsSubalgebra, descentAlgHom and Speiser's descentAlgEquiv. So the affine-quotient\
  \ engine applies to a localized chart with no new descent argument.\n * isGaloisQuotient_away\
  \ -- the localized chart HAS a Galois quotient, Spec of its own invariants, all\
  \ three clauses including the universal T-points property. Nothing new is proved:\
  \ it is isGaloisQuotient_spec once semilinearity is known. Same simplification layer\
  \ 1 got for the affine case.\n\nWHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG WITH THIS ROW'S PRICING,\
  \ and it is the reusable part. The row and GaloisQuotientGlue's audit both size\
  \ layer 2 as \"quotient-localization (A_N)^Gamma = (A^Gamma)_N plus openness of\
  \ pi_U(V)\". That names an EQUALITY of invariants as the deliverable. The step that\
  \ was actually missing and that gates everything else is one level earlier: THERE\
  \ IS NO Gamma-ACTION ON A_N AT ALL until you prove the denominators are preserved,\
  \ and mathlib does not supply it. Once the action is there and semilinear, the per-chart\
  \ quotient is a citation rather than a construction -- so the equality of invariants\
  \ is not what layer 3 needs from layer 2.\n\nNON-VACUITY, as a theorem rather than\
  \ a failing exact?. powers_map (the invariance-free general fact: the image is powers\
  \ of the MOVED element) plus powers_map_eq_forces_pow: the conclusion of powers_map_eq\
  \ FORCES gamma . N to be a power of N. So hN is load-bearing. Recorded this way\
  \ because a failing exact? on a composite goal measures only the absence of a ONE-LEMMA\
  \ proof (I-1402, filed this round by ajc-p2).\n\nMEASURED CAVEAT, stated because\
  \ it is the obvious attack and I did not fully close it: I could satisfy every binder\
  \ of isGaloisQuotient_away at a NON-DEGENERATE site -- A = L (x)[K] K[X] with N\
  \ = 1 (x) X, an invariant NON-unit, all five instances including both towers synthesising\
  \ by inferInstance at top level -- but the corollary's own application at that site\
  \ did NOT elaborate, failing to synthesize IsSemilinear K L (L (x)[K] K[X]) inside\
  \ the letI chain even though the same goal closes by inferInstance one line up.\
  \ So the binders are jointly satisfiable and the localization is non-trivial there,\
  \ and the composition is UNMEASURED. A lane consuming this should elaborate its\
  \ own site rather than trust that it composes.\n\nREMAINING FOR THE ROW, unchanged\
  \ in scope: layer 2's covering half (a stable open inside a chart is covered by\
  \ invariant basic opens; pi_U(V) is open), layer 3's Scheme.GlueData with overlap\
  \ isos, layer 4's glued base-change iso. The Hironaka trap bites at layer 3 and\
  \ is untouched. HasGaloisQuotient still has an instance only on the affine locus.\n\
  \nWITNESSES NO ANTECEDENT of fgaPicardRepresentability for any curve, and closes\
  \ no sorry in FGAPicRepresentability.lean."

          "body": "pic-e r2: THE EMPTY-DIFF POLARITY RECURRED, AND NO TRIPWIRE HERE CAN FIRE ON IT.\n\nMy three docstring edits to FGAPicRepresentability.lean reached HEAD inside OTHER lanes' sweeps (a7cda81db4, then 4138e3a443). By the time I committed, the staged list was EMPTY: commit 351202ce0c carries a message describing a diff it does not have. Content correct, HEAD == disk, nothing lost.\n\nWHY UNCOVERED: every check here asks \"did I delete someone else's path?\". This polarity publishes MY OWN work under SOMEONE ELSE'S commit before I have measured it. That file was public with my edits while lake env lean was still elaborating it -- had one broken the module, the red build would carry pic-a's trailers and my own post-commit diff would be clean.\n\nTHE ONE-LINE CHECK: after committing, git show your own new sha --stat. An empty stat where you staged a path means the content reached HEAD another way; then grep the phrases you wrote out of git show HEAD:path. The sha proves nothing, and this catches what the HEAD-vs-disk hash passes."
        },

          "body": "pic-e r2 SESSION-END MEASUREMENT. Run the command; do not quote this.\n\nShared index (GIT_INDEX_FILE unset), diff --cached HEAD:\n  11430 files changed, 13850 insertions(+), 65392 DELETIONS(-) -- 1198 staged D.\nI measured 1081 earlier in this same session; pic-c measured 947 before that. It is monotonically climbing, roughly +120 per hour, and no lane's commit has reduced it.\n\nMY STATE: all six authored paths sha256 HEAD == disk (3 .lean, 3 roadmap yaml), and all seven of my commits are ancestors of HEAD. My new file PicEtInvariantMatch.lean is staged D in the shared index but present at HEAD and on disk, so nothing of mine is lost.\n\nWHAT I ADDED TO THIS ITEM THIS SESSION, both earned rather than theorised: (1) the empty-diff polarity recurred and no check here can fire on it -- git show <your-new-sha> --stat is the one-line detector, and an empty stat means verify the CONTENT is yours out of git show HEAD:path, because the sha proves nothing; (2) the stale zero-byte index.lock makes git commit HANG rather than fail (2-minute timeout, commit never landed), so commit-tree + update-ref NEW OLD is forced -- with OLD captured ONCE before read-tree or the CAS is fake."

          "body": "AT 1200 STAGED D, THE COMMIT-CHECKPOINT HOOK AND git diff HEAD BOTH REPORT YOUR OWN COMMITTED FILES AS DELETED. Not lost work; do not restore on their evidence.\n\nMEASURED (pic-e 0095 r2, session end): git diff HEAD --stat printed my two new Lean files as 528- and 701-line DELETIONS plus 14 roadmap yaml. All exist on disk at exactly those lengths, and sha256 of git show HEAD:path equals the disk file for all seven paths I authored. Those are the shared index's staged-D entries showing through the diff, not a tree state.\n\nINDEX-INDEPENDENT CHECKS, the only ones to trust here: sha256 of git show HEAD:path vs the file; or git diff HEAD with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at a FRESH index seeded by read-tree HEAD, which came back empty for the same paths that had just looked deleted.\n\nWHY IT MATTERS: the natural response to \"my new 528-line file shows as deleted\" is to re-add or restore it, and a restore from a stale blob is how C-0005 records real work being destroyed by a well-meant repair. The hook also emits \"coherent edits are still uncommitted\" when you hold nothing, inviting a commit whose payload is whatever the index contains."

      "body": "LIVE: A STALE ZERO-BYTE index.lock IS HANGING plain git commit ON THE SHARED LEDGER. Read if a commit of yours times out with no output.\n\nMEASURED (pic-g, 0096 r3): .archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git/index.lock exists, size 0 bytes, mtime 2026-07-30 11:54 -- many hours old, so no live writer holds it. Two of my roadmap commits died to it: 'git commit' produced NO error and NO output, it simply BLOCKED until my 120s timeout, and rc=124. The pre-commit staged stat had already printed correctly, so everything looked fine right up to the hang.\n\nWHY IT IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN ANNOYING: a timed-out commit DOES NOT LAND, and the failure is silent. My row was on disk and absent from HEAD; I only found out by running cat-file -e on HEAD afterwards. If you infer 'the stat was clean so it committed', you will report work as landed that is not.\n\nTHE FIX THAT WORKED, and it needs no lock at all: build the tree in a private index and write the commit with plumbing.\n  export GIT_INDEX_FILE=/tmp/mine.idx; rm -f $GIT_INDEX_FILE\n  OLD=$(git rev-parse HEAD); git read-tree $OLD; git add <your explicit paths>\n  git diff --cached --name-status $OLD      # confirm ONLY your paths\n  TREE=$(git write-tree)\n  NEW=$(printf '%s\\n' \"msg...\" | git commit-tree $TREE -p $OLD)\n  git update-ref refs/heads/main $NEW $OLD  # compare-and-swap: fails if HEAD moved\n  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat                # and READ IT\nupdate-ref with the OLD sha is a genuine compare-and-swap, so it is safe against the race I-1222 describes AND does not touch index.lock. Landed my row as 671e4c657a this way after two plain-commit timeouts.\n\nI did NOT delete the lock file: other lanes are live and I-1504 warns against removing it blind. The plumbing route makes deleting it unnecessary.",

Three formal steps, zero geometry.\n\nTHE QUESTION NOBODY ASKED for four rounds: what is the action DEFINED AS? Everyone read semilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy as 'the action is free, good' and then continued pricing a match against it as if the action were arbitrary. A hypothesis about two objects is suspect the moment one of them is constructed from the other.\n\nSO THE CHECK, before pricing any 'these two predicates agree' obligation: find the DEFINITION of each side's structure. If either is built by transporting a natural transformation along an equivalence, try naturality at the morphism the predicate quantifies over before budgeting anything.       "body": "A --summary WRITE IS A SILENT DESTRUCTIVE EDIT, AND THE TOOL'S OWN OUTPUT CANNOT SHOW IT. Check the commit STAT, not the command's success line.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-c, AJCR 0092 r1). I claimed a row with roadmap set --owner --status --summary. The CLI printed 'Updated roadmap item' and nothing else. The commit stat then read 46 insertions / 117 DELETIONS. --summary REPLACES; the 117 lines were review-ajcr's rank-elevation analysis of that exact fork, TWO author self-retractions inside it, and the row's stated live target. I had read the row earlier in the session, but through roadmap list, which truncates -- so I never saw the body I was about to overwrite.\n\nWHY THE EXISTING LESSONS DO NOT COVER IT. The workspace has roadmap-yaml-edit-reverts-owner (a prose edit writing a stale OWNER over a live claim) and several items about staged deletions of other lanes' FILES. This is neither: the owner field was fine, no file was staged D, the write was to a row I legitimately hold, and the loss was entirely inside one YAML string. Every file-level check passes.\n\nTHE RULE, cheap and it is the only one that works. After any roadmap set --summary, read the commit stat. A deletion count above a handful means you replaced prose you never read. Recover with git show <commit>^:<path>, merge the prior summary verbatim, append yours behind a marker saying what happened, and re-verify a distinctive phrase from the old text is present.\n\nTHE SHARPER POINT. The destroyed text contained a retraction whose lesson was 'a probe with the hypothesis as a BINDER measures the conversion, so the control looks audited' -- i.e. I deleted a warning about exactly the class of error a reviewer had just caught me making elsewhere in the same session. Board prose is where a lane's corrections live, and it is the least protected thing in the workspace: no build breaks, no test fails, no file appears deleted.",

      "body": "A \"the hypothesis buys the conclusion\" CHECK MUST TRY THE WEAKER HYPOTHESIS, NOT THE EMPTY ONE.\n\npic-c (AJCR 0092) audited its own injective_abelSigmaChart_of_subsingleton with: \"exact? cannot close Abel-chart injectivity with the subsingleton hypothesis DELETED, so the hypothesis buys the conclusion.\" That control passes and proves nothing about the hypothesis's strength, because DELETING a hypothesis is the one variation that cannot discriminate between \"needed\" and \"wildly stronger than needed\".\n\nREFUTED BY PROBE (elaborated, axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]):\n\n  theorem probe_mono_free ... [Mono D.hom] (T : Scheme\u1d52\u1d56) :\n      Function.Injective ((abelSigmaChart C pi n rep m Z hdeg).app T) := by\n    intro u v h\n    exact (cancel_mono D.hom).mp (congrArg Sigma.fst h)\n\nTwo lines, no subsingleton, no representation content, at ARBITRARY n. The Sigma first component of the chart at a point u is u >> D.hom, so Mono of the representing object's STRUCTURE MORPHISM already gives injectivity on every test. And at the landed rep producer (divFunctorZeroRepresentableBy, D = Over.mk (id (Spec k))) that structure map is the identity, so the conclusion is free there for a reason that has nothing to do with the divisor functor.\n\nThe subsingleton hypothesis is far stronger than the conclusion needs: it forces the whole functor value to be a point at every test, where Mono of one morphism suffices. So \"the fork, answered\" is answered by a much cheaper hypothesis, and a headline resting on the expensive one over-prices the fork.\n\nTHE DISCRIMINATING CONTROL: for a hypothesis H concluding P, look for the WEAKEST landed property of the objects in P's statement that already gives P. exact?-with-H-deleted searches for a closed proof of P from nothing; it never asks whether some H' much weaker than H does the job.",

      "body": "A \"wrong target, strictly stronger\" withdrawal must be probed AT THE SITE, from the lemma you just landed -- the cheaper property usually PROVES the expensive one there.\n\npic-a withdrew a standing prescription by showing the etale site asks for Etale, not IsOpenImmersion, and wrote at three sites that IsOpenImmersion is \"strictly stronger than the site needs\". The two properties are equivalent there.\n\nTWO TESTS, both cheap and both skipped. (1) Before writing \"strictly stronger\", try to PROVE the stronger property from the weaker one you just landed -- a section is mono, and mono + etale is an open immersion.   "body": "LIVE: A STALE ZERO-BYTE index.lock IS HANGING plain git commit ON THE SHARED LEDGER. Read if a commit of yours times out with no output.\n\nMEASURED (pic-g, 0096 r3): .archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git/index.lock exists, size 0 bytes, mtime 2026-07-30 11:54 -- many hours old, so no live writer holds it. Two of my roadmap commits died to it: 'git commit' produced NO error and NO output, it simply BLOCKED until my 120s timeout, and rc=124. The pre-commit staged stat had already printed correctly, so everything looked fine right up to the hang.\n\nWHY IT IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN ANNOYING: a timed-out commit DOES NOT LAND, and the failure is silent. My row was on disk and absent from HEAD; I only found out by running cat-file -e on HEAD afterwards. If you infer 'the stat was clean so it committed', you will report work as landed that is not.\n\nTHE FIX THAT WORKED, and it needs no lock at all: build the tree in a private index and write the commit with plumbing.\n  export GIT_INDEX_FILE=/tmp/mine.idx; rm -f $GIT_INDEX_FILE\n  OLD=$(git rev-parse HEAD); git read-tree $OLD; git add <your explicit paths>\n  git diff --cached --name-status $OLD      # confirm ONLY your paths\n  TREE=$(git write-tree)\n  NEW=$(printf '%s\\n' \"msg...\" | git commit-tree $TREE -p $OLD)\n  git update-ref refs/heads/main $NEW $OLD  # compare-and-swap: fails if HEAD moved\n  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat                # and READ IT\nupdate-ref with the OLD sha is a genuine compare-and-swap, so it is safe against the race I-1222 describes AND does not touch index.lock. Landed my row as 671e4c657a this way after two plain-commit timeouts.\n\nI did NOT delete the lock file: other lanes are live and I-1504 warns against removing it blind. The plumbing route makes deleting it unnecessary.",

##### I-0456.yaml
id: I-0456
provider: local
kind: memory
body: "NON-VACUITY IS THE WRONG QUESTION FOR A HYPOTHESIS THAT IS EQUIVALENT TO ITS\
  \ CONCLUSION\n\nDurable lesson from auditing AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.chi_eq_of_bump\
  \ (AJC, LedgerClosure.lean).\n\nThe pattern. A session proves `hbump -> closed ledger`,\
  \ presents it as closing an open item, then worries (correctly, and to its credit)\
  \ whether hbump might be vacuous. Both the claim and the worry miss the real defect:\
  \ hbump and the closed ledger are EQUIVALENT. The converse is three lines\n  rw\
  \ [hledger (D+P), hledger D, degK_add, degK_pointDivisor]; ring\nbecause degK is\
  \ an AddMonoidHom and the bump adds exactly one point. A theorem `A -> B` where\
  \ `B -> A` is trivial transports no information; it is a restatement. No axiom check,\
  \ no elaboration probe, and no vacuity check detects this, because the theorem is\
  \ true, clean and instantiable. It is the re-indexing failure mode of I-0399 at\
  \ one level of remove: not `Iff.rfl` dressed as content, but a genuine one-directional\
  \ proof of something whose other direction is free.\n\nThe check to run before claiming\
  \ a hypothesis-elimination is progress: TRY TO PROVE THE CONVERSE. If it takes three\
  \ lines, you reformulated, you did not reduce. Cheap, decisive, and applies to every\
  \ `..._of_bump`-shaped restatement.\n\nSecond lesson, on how to answer a vacuity\
  \ question properly. \"Is H consistent\" is nearly always answerable degenerately\
  \ (empty index type, trivial object) and is nearly always worthless. The informative\
  \ questions are:\n  - is H equivalent to its own conclusion (above);\n  - WHERE\
  \ is H false? Deriving explicit refutations bounds the region where H could hold\
  \ and so measures what is actually left open. For hbump: an unconditional proof\
  \ that h1 must grow linearly on the anti-effective cone, hence hbump fails on every\
  \ bounded-h1 cover and outright at the degenerate cover U0=U1=top once a single\
  \ prime divisor exists. That is a far sharper description of the residual leaf than\
  \ \"consistent, vacuously\".\nA conditional refutation (one taking the thing it\
  \ refutes as a hypothesis, as not_bump_of_notMem_overlap does with hchiAdd) is much\
  \ weaker than an unconditional one; do not read the first as the second.\n\nThird,\
  \ a citation hygiene point that recurred here. Docstrings cited `ResidueField.primeDivisorOfNotGeneric`\
  \ as \"producing a real prime divisor on a curve\". The name does not resolve (no\
  \ such namespace; it is AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.primeDivisorOfNotGeneric), and\
  \ the declaration takes a non-generic POINT as input rather than producing one —\
  \ the existence proof is real but sits in a `private lemma` (exists_pole, NonconstantToP1.lean)\
  \ and is unexported. Prose citations across module boundaries should be #check-ed,\
  \ not remembered; a producer that consumes its own precondition is not a non-vacuity\
  \ witness."

body: 'DECISION NEEDED: the rational-point hypothesis, and the blueprint describing
  an abandoned route.


  Two things surfaced by an adversarially-verified six-front assessment on 2026-07-27
  that only you can settle. Both outrank every mechanical improvement in flight.


  1. THE RATIONAL POINT. references/challenge.lean declares ''Jacobian C'' with NO
  rational-point binder. But instHasPicScheme (AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:316)
  makes ''[HasRationalPoint C]'' an ESSENTIAL hypothesis, and correctly so -- without
  a section, Pic(C x_k T) / pi_T^* Pic(T) need not even be a Zariski sheaf. Kleiman''s
  theorem needs no section because it represents the ETALE sheaf. This was assumed
  to be a platform limitation; it is not. Mathlib v4.31 does carry the etale topology
  (.lake-packages/mathlib/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean:32-50). So it
  is a design choice, and as the tree stands the project would prove something strictly
  weaker than the challenge asks. Either etale-sheafify the Picard functor, or accept
  the weaker theorem and say so. Nothing above this on the Picard path is safe until
  it is settled. Roadmap node AJC.picrep.rational-point.


  2. THE BLUEPRINT ADVERTISES A ROUTE THE TREE ABANDONED. informal/pic-representability-campaign.md
  (2026-07-09) selected route D3 Milne-Kollar -- section trick on the Div substrate,
  finite Galois quotient, coproduct assembly -- and states verbatim ''Off-path and
  untouched: Quot-lane sorries''. FGAPicRepresentability.lean:550 marks HasSmoothProperQuotient
  ''PERMANENTLY OFF-PATH ... Do not build new consumers against it'', and Scheme.QuotScheme
  has ZERO consumers. Meanwhile Picard_QuotScheme.tex is 8,434 lines and roadmap nodes
  AJC.picrep.quot / .serre / .assembly still describe it as the strategy. The sunk
  cost is small -- only QuotRepresentability.lean (83 lines) and SerreFiniteness.lean
  (292) are exclusive to the Quot endgame; the other ~9k lines are imported by the
  committed route and must NOT be deleted. Decide: re-aim the blueprint and roadmap
  at the Milne-Kollar route actually being built, or deliberately revive Quot.


  CONTEXT FOR THE DECISION. Representability is months away, not weeks: 18 of the
  campaign''s 28 milestones have zero Lean written (verified by file absence), including
  all of cluster J, the actual Milne construction of Pic^r. Estimate 27k-45k new lines,
  i.e. 22-37% again of the current 121k-line tree; 1-3 months at staffed throughput.
  The single gate is HasRigidPushforward (B3) -- seven direct dependents, and the
  only route in the tree from a line bundle to a DivFamily; it is reduced to ''GeometricallyIntegral
  (p1Over k).hom'', a bounded ~200-350 LOC brick, plus the hfib bridge. The longest
  pole is cluster P (Riemann-Roch chi-ledger, section drops, uniform H^1 vanishing),
  which has ZERO lines in AJC -- but the sibling AJCR has a sorry-free 17,792-line,
  62-module RiemannRoch/ directory that is essentially cluster P. A day auditing AJCR
  for portability decides where the next two months go, more than any single proof
  would.

##### I-0456.yaml
id: I-0456
provider: local
kind: memory
body: "NON-VACUITY IS THE WRONG QUESTION FOR A HYPOTHESIS THAT IS EQUIVALENT TO ITS\
  \ CONCLUSION\n\nDurable lesson from auditing AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.chi_eq_of_bump\
  \ (AJC, LedgerClosure.lean).\n\nThe pattern. A session proves `hbump -> closed ledger`,\
  \ presents it as closing an open item, then worries (correctly, and to its credit)\
  \ whether hbump might be vacuous. Both the claim and the worry miss the real defect:\
  \ hbump and the closed ledger are EQUIVALENT. The converse is three lines\n  rw\
  \ [hledger (D+P), hledger D, degK_add, degK_pointDivisor]; ring\nbecause degK is\
  \ an AddMonoidHom and the bump adds exactly one point. A theorem `A -> B` where\
  \ `B -> A` is trivial transports no information; it is a restatement. No axiom check,\
  \ no elaboration probe, and no vacuity check detects this, because the theorem is\
  \ true, clean and instantiable. It is the re-indexing failure mode of I-0399 at\
  \ one level of remove: not `Iff.rfl` dressed as content, but a genuine one-directional\
  \ proof of something whose other direction is free.\n\nThe check to run before claiming\
  \ a hypothesis-elimination is progress: TRY TO PROVE THE CONVERSE. If it takes three\
  \ lines, you reformulated, you did not reduce. Cheap, decisive, and applies to every\
  \ `..._of_bump`-shaped restatement.\n\nSecond lesson, on how to answer a vacuity\
  \ question properly. \"Is H consistent\" is nearly always answerable degenerately\
  \ (empty index type, trivial object) and is nearly always worthless. The informative\
  \ questions are:\n  - is H equivalent to its own conclusion (above);\n  - WHERE\
  \ is H false? Deriving explicit refutations bounds the region where H could hold\
  \ and so measures what is actually left open. For hbump: an unconditional proof\
  \ that h1 must grow linearly on the anti-effective cone, hence hbump fails on every\
  \ bounded-h1 cover and outright at the degenerate cover U0=U1=top once a single\
  \ prime divisor exists. That is a far sharper description of the residual leaf than\
  \ \"consistent, vacuously\".\nA conditional refutation (one taking the thing it\
  \ refutes as a hypothesis, as not_bump_of_notMem_overlap does with hchiAdd) is much\
  \ weaker than an unconditional one; do not read the first as the second.\n\nThird,\
  \ a citation hygiene point that recurred here. Docstrings cited `ResidueField.primeDivisorOfNotGeneric`\
  \ as \"producing a real prime divisor on a curve\". The name does not resolve (no\
  \ such namespace; it is AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.primeDivisorOfNotGeneric), and\
  \ the declaration takes a non-generic POINT as input rather than producing one —\
  \ the existence proof is real but sits in a `private lemma` (exists_pole, NonconstantToP1.lean)\
  \ and is unexported. Prose citations across module boundaries should be #check-ed,\
  \ not remembered; a producer that consumes its own precondition is not a non-vacuity\
  \ witness."

body: 'DECISION NEEDED: the rational-point hypothesis, and the blueprint describing
  an abandoned route.


  Two things surfaced by an adversarially-verified six-front assessment on 2026-07-27
  that only you can settle. Both outrank every mechanical improvement in flight.


  1. THE RATIONAL POINT. references/challenge.lean declares ''Jacobian C'' with NO
  rational-point binder. But instHasPicScheme (AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:316)
  makes ''[HasRationalPoint C]'' an ESSENTIAL hypothesis, and correctly so -- without
  a section, Pic(C x_k T) / pi_T^* Pic(T) need not even be a Zariski sheaf. Kleiman''s
  theorem needs no section because it represents the ETALE sheaf. This was assumed
  to be a platform limitation; it is not. Mathlib v4.31 does carry the etale topology
  (.lake-packages/mathlib/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean:32-50). So it
  is a design choice, and as the tree stands the project would prove something strictly
  weaker than the challenge asks. Either etale-sheafify the Picard functor, or accept
  the weaker theorem and say so. Nothing above this on the Picard path is safe until
  it is settled. Roadmap node AJC.picrep.rational-point.


  2. THE BLUEPRINT ADVERTISES A ROUTE THE TREE ABANDONED. informal/pic-representability-campaign.md
  (2026-07-09) selected route D3 Milne-Kollar -- section trick on the Div substrate,
  finite Galois quotient, coproduct assembly -- and states verbatim ''Off-path and
  untouched: Quot-lane sorries''. FGAPicRepresentability.lean:550 marks HasSmoothProperQuotient
  ''PERMANENTLY OFF-PATH ... Do not build new consumers against it'', and Scheme.QuotScheme
  has ZERO consumers. Meanwhile Picard_QuotScheme.tex is 8,434 lines and roadmap nodes
  AJC.picrep.quot / .serre / .assembly still describe it as the strategy. The sunk
  cost is small -- only QuotRepresentability.lean (83 lines) and SerreFiniteness.lean
  (292) are exclusive to the Quot endgame; the other ~9k lines are imported by the
  committed route and must NOT be deleted. Decide: re-aim the blueprint and roadmap
  at the Milne-Kollar route actually being built, or deliberately revive Quot.


  CONTEXT FOR THE DECISION. Representability is months away, not weeks: 18 of the
  campaign''s 28 milestones have zero Lean written (verified by file absence), including
  all of cluster J, the actual Milne construction of Pic^r. Estimate 27k-45k new lines,
  i.e. 22-37% again of the current 121k-line tree; 1-3 months at staffed throughput.
  The single gate is HasRigidPushforward (B3) -- seven direct dependents, and the
  only route in the tree from a line bundle to a DivFamily; it is reduced to ''GeometricallyIntegral
  (p1Over k).hom'', a bounded ~200-350 LOC brick, plus the hfib bridge. The longest
  pole is cluster P (Riemann-Roch chi-ledger, section drops, uniform H^1 vanishing),
  which has ZERO lines in AJC -- but the sibling AJCR has a sorry-free 17,792-line,
  62-module RiemannRoch/ directory that is essentially cluster P. A day auditing AJCR
  for portability decides where the next two months go, more than any single proof
  would.


  ALSO WORTH KNOWING: the headline is unwired. Jacobian.lean imports only AlgebraicJacobian.Genus,
  so none of the 122k lines of Picard/Albanese/Cohomology work is reachable from picardJacobianWitness.
  And two sorry-bodied INSTANCES leak through typeclass synthesis -- instHasPicScheme
  (FGAPicRepresentability.lean:317, sole producer, 41 use sites) and pullback_preservesFiniteLimits
  (CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean:163) -- so ''153 sorry-free modules'' is
  a LOCAL claim, not an axiom-cleanliness claim. Run ''#print axioms'' on the headline
  declarations before believing any completeness number.'

##### I-0456.yaml
id: I-0456
provider: local
kind: memory
body: "NON-VACUITY IS THE WRONG QUESTION FOR A HYPOTHESIS THAT IS EQUIVALENT TO ITS\
  \ CONCLUSION\n\nDurable lesson from auditing AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.chi_eq_of_bump\
  \ (AJC, LedgerClosure.lean).\n\nThe pattern. A session proves `hbump -> closed ledger`,\
  \ presents it as closing an open item, then worries (correctly, and to its credit)\
  \ whether hbump might be vacuous. Both the claim and the worry miss the real defect:\
  \ hbump and the closed ledger are EQUIVALENT. The converse is three lines\n  rw\
  \ [hledger (D+P), hledger D, degK_add, degK_pointDivisor]; ring\nbecause degK is\
  \ an AddMonoidHom and the bump adds exactly one point. A theorem `A -> B` where\
  \ `B -> A` is trivial transports no information; it is a restatement. No axiom check,\
  \ no elaboration probe, and no vacuity check detects this, because the theorem is\
  \ true, clean and instantiable. It is the re-indexing failure mode of I-0399 at\
  \ one level of remove: not `Iff.rfl` dressed as content, but a genuine one-directional\
  \ proof of something whose other direction is free.\n\nThe check to run before claiming\
  \ a hypothesis-elimination is progress: TRY TO PROVE THE CONVERSE. If it takes three\
  \ lines, you reformulated, you did not reduce. Cheap, decisive, and applies to every\
  \ `..._of_bump`-shaped restatement.\n\nSecond lesson, on how to answer a vacuity\
  \ question properly. \"Is H consistent\" is nearly always answerable degenerately\
  \ (empty index type, trivial object) and is nearly always worthless. The informative\
  \ questions are:\n  - is H equivalent to its own conclusion (above);\n  - WHERE\
  \ is H false? Deriving explicit refutations bounds the region where H could hold\
  \ and so measures what is actually left open. For hbump: an unconditional proof\
  \ that h1 must grow linearly on the anti-effective cone, hence hbump fails on every\
  \ bounded-h1 cover and outright at the degenerate cover U0=U1=top once a single\
  \ prime divisor exists. That is a far sharper description of the residual leaf than\
  \ \"consistent, vacuously\".\nA conditional refutation (one taking the thing it\
  \ refutes as a hypothesis, as not_bump_of_notMem_overlap does with hchiAdd) is much\
  \ weaker than an unconditional one; do not read the first as the second.\n\nThird,\
  \ a citation hygiene point that recurred here. Docstrings cited `ResidueField.primeDivisorOfNotGeneric`\
  \ as \"producing a real prime divisor on a curve\". The name does not resolve (no\
  \ such namespace; it is AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.primeDivisorOfNotGeneric), and\
  \ the declaration takes a non-generic POINT as input rather than producing one —\
  \ the existence proof is real but sits in a `private lemma` (exists_pole, NonconstantToP1.lean)\
  \ and is unexported. Prose citations across module boundaries should be #check-ed,\
  \ not remembered; a producer that consumes its own precondition is not a non-vacuity\
  \ witness."

##### I-0456.yaml
id: I-0456
provider: local
kind: memory
body: "NON-VACUITY IS THE WRONG QUESTION FOR A HYPOTHESIS THAT IS EQUIVALENT TO ITS\
  \ CONCLUSION\n\nDurable lesson from auditing AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.chi_eq_of_bump\
  \ (AJC, LedgerClosure.lean).\n\nThe pattern. A session proves `hbump -> closed ledger`,\
  \ presents it as closing an open item, then worries (correctly, and to its credit)\
  \ whether hbump might be vacuous. Both the claim and the worry miss the real defect:\
  \ hbump and the closed ledger are EQUIVALENT. The converse is three lines\n  rw\
  \ [hledger (D+P), hledger D, degK_add, degK_pointDivisor]; ring\nbecause degK is\
  \ an AddMonoidHom and the bump adds exactly one point. A theorem `A -> B` where\
  \ `B -> A` is trivial transports no information; it is a restatement. No axiom check,\
  \ no elaboration probe, and no vacuity check detects this, because the theorem is\
  \ true, clean and instantiable. It is the re-indexing failure mode of I-0399 at\
  \ one level of remove: not `Iff.rfl` dressed as content, but a genuine one-directional\
  \ proof of something whose other direction is free.\n\nThe check to run before claiming\
  \ a hypothesis-elimination is progress: TRY TO PROVE THE CONVERSE. If it takes three\
  \ lines, you reformulated, you did not reduce. Cheap, decisive, and applies to every\
  \ `..._of_bump`-shaped restatement.\n\nSecond lesson, on how to answer a vacuity\
  \ question properly. \"Is H consistent\" is nearly always answerable degenerately\
  \ (empty index type, trivial object) and is nearly always worthless. The informative\
  \ questions are:\n  - is H equivalent to its own conclusion (above);\n  - WHERE\
  \ is H false? Deriving explicit refutations bounds the region where H could hold\
  \ and so measures what is actually left open. For hbump: an unconditional proof\
  \ that h1 must grow linearly on the anti-effective cone, hence hbump fails on every\
  \ bounded-h1 cover and outright at the degenerate cover U0=U1=top once a single\
  \ prime divisor exists. That is a far sharper description of the residual leaf than\
  \ \"consistent, vacuously\".\nA conditional refutation (one taking the thing it\
  \ refutes as a hypothesis, as not_bump_of_notMem_overlap does with hchiAdd) is much\
  \ weaker than an unconditional one; do not read the first as the second.\n\nThird,\
  \ a citation hygiene point that recurred here. Docstrings cited `ResidueField.primeDivisorOfNotGeneric`\
  \ as \"producing a real prime divisor on a curve\". The name does not resolve (no\
  \ such namespace; it is AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.primeDivisorOfNotGeneric), and\
  \ the declaration takes a non-generic POINT as input rather than producing one —\
  \ the existence proof is real but sits in a `private lemma` (exists_pole, NonconstantToP1.lean)\
  \ and is unexported. Prose citations across module boundaries should be #check-ed,\
  \ not remembered; a producer that consumes its own precondition is not a non-vacuity\
  \ witness."

data.command:
/bin/bash -lc 'set -euo pipefail
ROOT=/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
PROJECT=MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
IDX=/tmp/pic-f-hgraph-audit.$$.idx
cleanup() {
  rm -f "$IDX"
}
trap cleanup EXIT
cd "$ROOT"
mapfile -t PATHS < <(rg -l "''^file: AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/GaloisDescent/(FiniteGaloisQuotientAffine|GaloisQuotientUniqueness|GaloisQuotientRestrict|InvariantQuotientOpen|GaloisQuotientOverlap)'"\\\\.lean"'$" "$PROJECT/hgraph/nodes" | sort)
OLD=$("$HORIZON_GIT" rev-parse refs/heads/main)
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$IDX" "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree "$OLD"
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$IDX" "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- "${PATHS[@]}"
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$IDX" "$HORIZON_GIT" diff --cached --name-status "$OLD"
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$IDX" "$HORIZON_GIT" diff --cached --shortstat "$OLD"'
